rows.h: Modf(cal L); t∈cal L; no internal deletions; tot. ord.
rows.shows: The f is full height, Ls have looped bases, and two cancellations remain within the set builder. The left cancelled glyph is a dark overwritten blob; the other retains the S, union and brace outlines. No final point follows ord.
Two short high quote strokes occur at both ends, not angled guillemets. The last connector is cut by the right edge and remains unresolved.

rows.place: first subscripts in enumeration and components
rows.shows: The small subscript has a p-like closed head and descending stroke, sometimes thickly retraced. There is no securely separable deleted 0 and live 1, so the revision layer asserted by C is replaced by an explicit glyph doubt.
rows.consequential: The first subscripts are recorded as unresolved p/1/0 glyphs, without inventing a cancelled 0 layer.

rows.shows: A small comma is visible after s₂ before the next inequality; there is no point after ens.

Both end Ls have looped feet. The first left bracket is heavily retraced over a possible L, while the last internal pair has clear square brackets facing inward. These surprising closed brackets are retained.

rows.shows: The n=1 lead-in is a short wave rather than a clearly formed cas. At n≥2 the word after the article has an s, long u/i run and tall t; no separate qui est can be seen. The crossed une remains uncertain.

A separate acute is above the e of dé. The cancelled word begins ord with a tall d; the live word has b-i-o-r-d-r-e. The parenthesis uses singular la structure.
rows.consequential: The recovered structure is called biordre, not binaire.
